page: Amazon Web Services c8g.12xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. The configuration provisions 48 dedicated physical cores with 48 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 96.0 GB, providing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage, depending entirely on network-attached volumes, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core throughput and memory system performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 395.06 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 184.52 GB/sec, as well as PassMark memory score and database operations. Computational tests show top-tier execution in Geekbench multi-core workloads and Clang software compilation, alongside strong performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput of 102.14 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core evaluations—including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics—score within average ranges.

With its 1:2 memory ratio and absence of bundled local NVMe storage, the architecture delivers favorable cost efficiency for horizontal compute jobs that can leverage high multi-core parallelism and memory throughput without requiring expansive RAM allocations. It is well suited for distributed build systems, Clang-based software compilation, batch processing pipelines, web serving at scale, and parallel compute tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.12xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized virtual server configured with 48 dedicated physical cores running on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 hardware at 2.8 GHz. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 96.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps, while including no dedicated GPUs or local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier performance in multi-core metrics, software compilation using Clang, static web serving throughput, and large-block memory read and write bandwidth. Single-threaded metrics land in the middle tier, reflecting an architecture focused on parallel throughput. The c8g.12xlarge offers an efficient compute-per-core profile tailored for parallel compilation, batch compute pipelines, containerized microservices, and high-throughput web serving architectures.
